claims.text: The initial equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy is homogeneous and single-phase.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy has disordered grain boundaries.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy has high toughness.
Annealing CoCrFeMnNi at 700–750 °C for 10–30 minutes promotes atomic reorganization at its grain boundaries.
The specified annealing treatment induces a grain-boundary complexion transition from a disordered state to an ordered interfacial film.
The ordered grain-boundary film is intrinsically more brittle than the initial disordered boundary structure.
Formation of the ordered interfacial film reduces grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesive strength lowers the fracture toughness of the alloy and causes embrittlement.
The 700–750 °C, 10–30 minute treatment can produce the proposed boundary transition without causing a bulk phase transformation.
Ordered interfacial films will be observable in annealed and quenched samples by high-resolution TEM and grain-boundary spectroscopy.
Annealed and quenched samples will have lower fracture toughness than the as-quenched baseline.
The predicted toughness reduction will be especially evident under higher applied stress.
The embrittling complexion transition is confined to a narrow treatment window of 700–750 °C for 10–30 minutes.
Annealing outside the stated temperature or time window may not induce the same complexion transition.
Prolonged annealing may cause precipitation rather than an isolated grain-boundary complexion transition.
Embrittlement in conventional alloys typically results from grain-boundary segregation or precipitate formation.
